# OpenAPI review notes

## Generated file and verification

`docs/public/openapi.json` is generated by `just openapi`. Do not edit it by hand. The exporter reads Swift declarations without starting Relay.
`.gitattributes` marks this JSON file as generated for GitHub reviews.

Swift package tests cover schema generation and document structure.
Relay contract tests cover HTTP behavior and compare the generated schemas with real encoded fixtures.
`just check-openapi` detects a stale generated artifact.
The documentation uses `pnpm check` and `pnpm build`, without a separate Node test suite.

## How the renderer works

`createReference` prepares the page data once during the Astro build.
A reference index caches pointer lookups, and a schema index caches prepared schemas and repeated reference nodes.
The Astro components receive typed display data rather than repeatedly walking the OpenAPI document.

Headers that are identical on every response appear once per operation.
Responses with identical content and remaining headers share a body section, but retain each status code and description.
References link to component definitions instead of expanding recursively.

The OpenAPI types come from the OpenAPI 3.2 module of `openapi3-ts`.
Hono's `@hono/zod-openapi` also uses that package for its OpenAPI types.
The vendored declarations have a pinned source revision and the upstream MIT license in `docs/src/vendor/openapi3-ts/`.
No runtime package was added.

## What JSONResponse and relayJSONResponse do

`JSONResponse<Value>` carries a typed model, an HTTP status, and a renderer closure.
The type lets `JSONEndpoint<Value>` reject a handler with a different success model at compile time.
Hummingbird later calls the wrapper to produce the actual HTTP response.
The wrapper calls the supplied renderer and makes sure that its resulting status matches the handler's status.

`relayJSONResponse` connects that wrapper to the existing `jsonResponse` helper.
It preserves RelayJSON serialization, the status, and X-Request-ID.
It does not add schema validation or change message delivery.

`CaseIterable` on `MessageSearchMode` serves one purpose: the documented `search_mode` enum comes from `allCases`.
A new accepted case then appears in the documentation without another list to update.
It does not change query parsing or the existing raw values.

## Inspect the event enum

`@OpenAPISchema` adds a schema-provider conformance to `RelayEventType`.
Components enter a document when its endpoints reference them.
This enum is not currently exported as a standalone `RelayEventType_response` component.
The event names are visible as individual constants at this JSON path:

```text
paths["/v1/events"].get.responses["200"].content["text/event-stream"]
  .itemSchema.oneOf[*].properties.event.const
```

The seven event variants contain those constants. The eighth variant describes the initial retry control.
Payload components such as `StreamReadyEvent_response` appear under `components.schemas`.
The generated reference displays both the event constants and links to the payload definitions.

Run this focused test to compare every enum value with the exported frame definitions and actual encoded event fixtures:

```sh
swift test --filter openAPISSEPayloadsMatchAllEmittedEventShapes
```

To inspect the enum's generated schema separately, this Swift snippet uses the existing API:

```swift
import Foundation
import HummingbirdOpenAPIModels
import RelayCore

let registry = SchemaContext()
_ = try registry.schema(for: RelayEventType.self, direction: .response)
let data = try RelayJSON.encoder.encode(registry.components)
FileHandle.standardOutput.write(data)
```

That output contains a `RelayEventType_response` component with the seven raw string values.
The compiler generates those values from the enum cases.
This is an isolated schema inspection, not a change to the exported Relay document.

## Put definitions beside their handlers

This works with the existing API. No new macro or package change is needed.
Move the static endpoint properties from `ConversationRoutes+OpenAPI.swift` into `ConversationRoutes.swift`, above their handlers.
The following example shows only the list operation:

```swift
import Hummingbird
import HummingbirdOpenAPI
import OpenAPIKit
import RelayCore

struct ConversationRoutes {
    let conversations: ConversationService

    static let listEndpoint = JSONEndpoint<PaginatedResponse<Conversation>>(
        method: .get,
        path: "/v1/conversations",
        operationID: "listConversations",
        summary: "Page through conversations.",
        tags: ["Conversations"],
        parameters: [
            V1OpenAPI.limit(default: 20),
            V1OpenAPI.cursor,
            V1OpenAPI.boolean("unread_only", description: "Return only conversations with unread messages."),
            .init(name: "participant", location: .query,
                  description: "Exact normalized phone number or email address.", schema: .string),
        ],
        responses: V1OpenAPI.responses(
            description: "A page of conversations.",
            errors: [.badRequest, .unprocessableContent, .serviceUnavailable]
        ),
        responseHeaders: V1OpenAPI.responseHeaders
    )

    func register(on router: Router<RelayRequestContext>) {
        Self.listEndpoint.register(on: router, use: list)
    }

    @Sendable private func list(
        _ request: Request,
        context: RelayRequestContext
    ) async throws -> JSONResponse<PaginatedResponse<Conversation>> {
        let participant = try V1Query.string(request, "participant").map(RecipientHandle.direct(value:))
        let page = try await conversations.list(
            limit: V1Query.limit(request, default: 20),
            cursor: V1Query.cursor(request),
            unreadOnly: V1Query.bool(request, "unread_only"),
            participant: participant
        )
        return relayJSONResponse(page, requestID: context.requestID)
    }
}
```

The metadata and handler then live together, but the route file becomes longer.
The same endpoint value still supplies live registration and export.
Keep it static and accessible within RelayServer so export needs no ConversationService instance.
The other endpoint properties and the `endpoints` collection can move into the same type without changing their callers.

A local definition inside `register` or a handler loses that property.
The exporter cannot reach it without constructing route dependencies or executing route setup.
An annotation directly on each handler is another option, but requires a new route macro and tests.
It must still receive query defaults, descriptions, and error responses explicitly because handler bodies do not reliably reveal them.

No route declarations were moved during this review revision. This example explains the option before changing the layout.

## Specification basis and limits

The representations follow [OpenAPI 3.2.1](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.1.html), not a Relay-specific document format.
The implementation covers the features that Relay needs. It does not claim to implement every OpenAPI feature.
The specification defines the structure. Swift declarations and existing behavior supply the API-specific facts.

The implementation uses these specification rules:

- [Schema Objects](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.1.html#schema-object) use JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. Field presence and nullability are separate.
- [Parameter Objects](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.1.html#parameter-object) describe query, path, and header values. Path parameters are required.
- [Binary data](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.1.html#working-with-binary-data) uses media types without pretending raw bytes are JSON strings.
- [Streaming media](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.1.html#streaming-sequential-media-types) uses `itemSchema`. SSE data remains a string with JSON content described by `contentSchema`.
- [Security Scheme Objects](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.1.html#security-scheme-object) describe the relay's HTTP bearer authentication.

OpenAPIKit checks document structure and references. It does not prove that every runtime value matches every schema.
The contract tests compare serialization and known responses with the generated description.
Business rules such as allowlist membership and normalized participant uniqueness remain in the existing services.

Custom codecs still need explicit schema rules or providers. The macro does not interpret arbitrary Swift codec bodies.
OpenAPIKit 7 lacks native `contentSchema` support, so the canonical encoder restores that standard keyword from an internal marker.
The final JSON contains the standard keyword, not a Relay-specific replacement.
